title: Tempest 2000
subtitle: A neon edge above the void
summary: Tempest 2000 is Jeff Minter's reworking of Atari's 1981 arcade shooter, first released for the Jaguar on 13 April 1994.
body: Tempest 2000 is Jeff Minter's reworking of Atari's 1981 arcade shooter, first released for the Jaguar on 13 April 1994. The player moves a claw-shaped Blaster around the rim of a geometric web, firing down its lanes at enemies climbing towards the edge. It preserves the original's spatial challenge while surrounding it with new effects, electronic music and power-ups. The action remains a matter of choosing the right lane at the right moment as the empty space below becomes increasingly crowded.

The campaign crosses one hundred webs with changing shapes, colors and enemy arrangements. Power-ups add abilities and rewards to the familiar circuit around the rim, while bonus sections interrupt the shooting with another kind of movement. New enemy types change the danger attached to each lane. The player has to read the whole web while reacting to the nearest threat, often moving past a promising target to stop something closer to the edge. Success unlocks a harder Beastly Mode, extending the challenge beyond the first complete run.

Developed by Llamasoft, the Jaguar version made Minter's interest in visual intensity and arcade scoring especially visible. Alastair Lindsay, Ian Howe and Kevin Saville supplied the soundtrack, giving the abstract battle a strong musical identity. Particles and bright colors amplify a design whose geometry remains essential to understanding the action. Later versions reached computers, Saturn and PlayStation, with changes between them. The original Jaguar release became one of the console's defining games through the close connection between its old arcade foundation and its exuberant presentation.
